description: This topic covers the meaning and characteristics of weeds, their harmful and beneficial effects, the classification of weeds, and the cultural, mechanical, biological and chemical methods used to control them.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following best describes a weed?

options.text: A plant that is deliberately grown for food
A plant growing where it is not wanted
A plant that only grows in a forest
A plant that cannot produce seeds

mcq.explanation: A weed is any plant that grows where it is not wanted by the farmer, competing with crops.

mcq.questionText: Which characteristic helps weeds survive better than many crops?

options.text: They produce large numbers of seeds
They die immediately in dry seasons

mcq.explanation: Most weeds produce large numbers of seeds, allowing them to spread and survive quickly.

mcq.questionText: A weed that completes its whole life cycle within one season is classified as a:
mcq.explanation: Annual weeds germinate, grow, flower, set seed and die within a single growing season.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a harmful effect of weeds on crops?

options.text: They compete with crops for water and nutrients

mcq.explanation: Weeds compete with crops for water, nutrients, light and space, reducing crop yield.

mcq.questionText: The control of weeds by uprooting them using hands is an example of which method?
mcq.explanation: Hand pulling, hoeing and slashing are mechanical (physical) methods of weed control.

mcq.questionText: Chemicals used to kill weeds are called:
mcq.explanation: Herbicides are chemicals specifically used to kill or control weeds.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an example of cultural weed control?

options.text: Releasing insects that feed on weeds

mcq.explanation: Cultural methods such as crop rotation, mulching and proper spacing prevent weeds from establishing.

mcq.questionText: Biological control of weeds involves the use of:

options.text: Living organisms such as insects or animals

mcq.explanation: Biological control uses living organisms, such as insects or grazing animals, that feed on weeds to reduce them.

mcq.questionText: Weeds such as grasses that have long, thin leaves with parallel veins are classified as:
mcq.explanation: Narrow-leaved weeds, mostly grasses, have long, thin leaves with parallel veins.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a beneficial effect of weeds?

options.text: They protect the soil from erosion when ploughed under
They block sunlight from reaching crops

mcq.explanation: Some weeds cover the soil surface and protect it from erosion, and can add organic matter when ploughed under.

mcq.questionText: A weed that takes two seasons to complete its life cycle is known as a:
mcq.explanation: Biennial weeds need two growing seasons; they grow vegetatively in the first and flower and seed in the second.

mcq.questionText: Why is it important to control weeds before they produce seeds?

options.text: To give them time to multiply
To prevent them from spreading to other areas

mcq.explanation: Controlling weeds before seeding prevents new seeds from being added to the soil, reducing future infestations.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a safety measure when handling herbicides?

options.text: Wearing protective clothing such as gloves and a mask

mcq.explanation: Protective clothing such as gloves, masks and overalls protects the user from harmful contact with herbicides.

mcq.questionText: A selective herbicide is one that:

options.text: Kills only certain types of weeds without harming the crop

mcq.explanation: A selective herbicide kills specific weeds, for example broad-leaved weeds, while leaving the crop unharmed.

mcq.questionText: Perennial weeds are usually more difficult to control than annual weeds mainly because they:

options.text: Have underground structures such as rhizomes and tubers that survive

mcq.explanation: Perennial weeds survive for many seasons through underground parts like rhizomes, tubers and roots, so they regrow even after the top is removed.

fib.questionText: A plant growing where it is not wanted is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A weed is any plant that grows where the farmer does not want it.

fib.questionText: Chemicals that are used to kill weeds are known as _____.
fib.explanation: Herbicides are chemical substances applied to control or kill weeds.

fib.questionText: A weed that completes its life cycle in one season is called an _____ weed.
fib.explanation: Annual weeds grow, flower, seed and die within a single season.

fib.questionText: Weeds compete with crops for water, light, space and _____.
fib.explanation: Competition for nutrients reduces the amount available to crops, lowering yield.

fib.questionText: Grasses with long, thin leaves and parallel veins are classified as _____ weeds.
fib.explanation: Narrow-leaved weeds are mostly grasses with parallel-veined leaves.

fib.questionText: The control of weeds using living organisms such as insects is called _____ control.
fib.explanation: Biological control uses natural enemies such as insects or animals to reduce weeds.

fib.questionText: A weed that takes two seasons to complete its life cycle is called a _____ weed.
fib.explanation: Biennial weeds grow vegetatively in the first season and flower and seed in the second.

fib.questionText: Hoeing, slashing and hand pulling are examples of _____ methods of weed control.
fib.explanation: Mechanical methods physically remove or destroy weeds using tools or hands.

fib.questionText: A herbicide that kills only certain weeds without harming the crop is described as _____.
fib.explanation: Selective herbicides target specific weeds while leaving the crop unharmed.

fib.questionText: Perennial weeds survive for many seasons through underground structures such as rhizomes and _____.
fib.explanation: Underground tubers, rhizomes and roots allow perennial weeds to regrow each season.

tf.questionText: A weed is any plant that grows where it is not wanted by the farmer.
tf.explanation: By definition a weed is an unwanted plant growing among crops.

tf.questionText: Weeds compete with crops for water, nutrients, light and space.
tf.explanation: This competition is one of the main harmful effects of weeds.

tf.questionText: Herbicides are chemicals used to kill insects in the field.
tf.explanation: Herbicides kill weeds; insecticides are the chemicals used to kill insects.

tf.questionText: Annual weeds complete their life cycle within one growing season.
tf.explanation: Annual weeds germinate, grow, flower, seed and die in a single season.

tf.questionText: Weeds have no beneficial effects at all in farming.
tf.explanation: Some weeds protect soil from erosion, add organic matter and can be used as fodder.

tf.questionText: Crop rotation and mulching are examples of cultural weed control methods.
tf.explanation: Cultural methods prevent weeds from establishing through good farming practices.

tf.questionText: Broad-leaved weeds have leaves with net-like (network) veins.
tf.explanation: Broad-leaved (dicot) weeds have wide leaves with network venation.

tf.questionText: Perennial weeds are easier to control than annual weeds.
tf.explanation: Perennial weeds are harder to control because their underground parts survive and regrow.

tf.questionText: Herbicides should be sprayed against the direction of the wind.
tf.explanation: One should spray with the wind at one's back to avoid breathing in the chemical drift.

tf.questionText: Controlling weeds before they produce seeds helps reduce future weed infestations.
tf.explanation: Removing weeds before seeding prevents new seeds from entering the soil.

summary.correctAnswer: A weed is any plant growing where it is not wanted.
summary.explanation: Weeds grow among crops and are not deliberately planted.

summary.correctAnswer: Weeds compete with crops for water, nutrients, light and space.
summary.explanation: This competition lowers crop yield and quality.

summary.correctAnswer: Weeds produce large numbers of seeds and grow fast.
summary.explanation: This helps them spread and survive easily.

summary.correctAnswer: Weeds may be annual, biennial or perennial.
summary.explanation: This grouping is based on how long a weed takes to complete its life cycle.

summary.correctAnswer: Weeds may be narrow-leaved or broad-leaved.
summary.explanation: Narrow-leaved weeds are mostly grasses; broad-leaved weeds have wide leaves.

summary.correctAnswer: Preventing weeds through good practices like crop rotation and mulching.
summary.explanation: These practices stop weeds from establishing in the field.

summary.correctAnswer: Physically removing weeds by hoeing, slashing or hand pulling.
summary.explanation: Tools or hands are used to destroy or remove weeds.

summary.correctAnswer: Using living organisms such as insects or animals to reduce weeds.
summary.explanation: Natural enemies feed on weeds and lower their numbers.

summary.correctAnswer: Killing weeds using chemicals called herbicides.
summary.explanation: Herbicides may be selective or non-selective.

summary.correctAnswer: Wear protective clothing, follow instructions and store chemicals safely.
summary.explanation: These measures protect the user, others and the environment from harm.

hoq.questionText: A maize farmer notices that a field heavily infested with perennial grasses keeps regrowing even after repeated hoeing. Which combination of measures is MOST likely to give long-term control?

options.text: Hand pulling the leaves only, once per season
Using a selective herbicide together with removing underground rhizomes
Leaving the weeds to set seed before slashing

hoq.explanation: Perennials regrow from underground parts, so combining a suitable herbicide with removal of rhizomes attacks both shoots and storage structures for lasting control.

hoq.questionText: A farmer wants to clear broad-leaved weeds from a maize crop without damaging the maize. The best choice would be to apply a herbicide that is:

options.text: Non-selective, killing all plants in the field
A fungicide applied to the soil

hoq.explanation: Maize is a narrow-leaved (grass) crop, so a selective herbicide targeting broad-leaved weeds removes the weeds while leaving the maize unharmed.

hoq.questionText: Why might over-reliance on chemical weed control alone be discouraged in favour of an integrated approach?

options.text: Herbicides are always cheaper than other methods
Continuous herbicide use can pollute the environment and weeds may develop resistance
Herbicides increase the number of weed seeds in the soil
Chemical control never kills any weeds

hoq.explanation: Relying only on herbicides can cause environmental pollution and lead to herbicide-resistant weeds, so combining methods (integrated weed management) is recommended.
